transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-01 15:00 UTC | Duration: 63m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Sara (Redwood CSM), Maya (Petalum), Ravi (Petalum CTO), Olivia (Platform Eng), Ethan (Security)

Summary: quick intro, alignment on network handoff, staging provisioning, security artifacts and initial perf bench plan. Topics: VPC peering, Dedicated vs Hosted, KMS and encryption, runbook, pilot pass/fail criteria.

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I know everybody's busy so we'll try to keep this tight. quick intros — Jordan's our SE who will own the infra side, Sara is customer success — she'll coordinate the onboarding runway.
00:32 Maya: Hi hi, thanks. we just spun up some early tests but want to formalize the pilot and get staging keys. we're targeting end of month for a small pilot.
00:48 Jordan: Cool. quick note — we usually recommend starting in hosted to validate prompts then move to Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and isolation. that said if you need VPC/on-prem we can plan that too.
01:10 Ravi: For us isolation and auditability matter — we need KMS integration and SAML SSO. also, is there an audit log stream we can ship into our SIEM?
01:26 Sara: Yep — we have audit logs, token-level traces, and we can provide the retention options. i'll include the export format in the artifacts.
01:44 Ethan: on KMS — do you support customer-managed keys and HSM-backed keys? and what's the encryption-at-rest story for dedicated?
02:00 Jordan: We support customer-managed KMS across Private and Dedicated. for hosted there's envelope encryption and we can work through a bring-your-own key flow for Private. sorry if i said "dedicate" before — typo — but the features map to Dedicated/Private.
02:22 Alex: ok jumping into the network handoff: Olivia we need your IP ranges and any restrictions so we can open peering. we can do either VPC peering or VPN depending on your network team.
02:40 Olivia: We'll do VPC peering if possible, our security team prefers that. i'll grab the IP blocks and a contact for neteng.
02:52 Jordan: Great. on the perf side, can you share representative prompt lengths and 95th latency SLOs? that'll help us size a dedicated pool or recommend batching settings/quantization.
03:12 Maya: typical prompts are 120-300 tokens, 95th we want sub-500ms for short turn completions, but open to tradeoffs if cost is high.
03:30 Jordan: Got it. sub-500ms is doable for smaller models in Dedicated with tuned batching and prefix caching. we'll run a benchmark once staging keys are in. note: our "KV cache" and prefix cache can reduce repeated context cost but it's sensitive to prompt fan-out.
03:55 Ravi: can Redwood route across regions? we have users in EU and US and want to minimize cross-region latency.
04:06 Alex: Yes, Smart routing can pin traffic by region and fallback when capacity is constrained. i'll include the region map in the doc pack.
04:20 Ethan: about compliance — SOC2, ISO? and do you provide pen test reports?
04:28 Sara: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO docs. pen test summaries are available on request. we'll send these in the security bundle.
04:42 Maya: cool. operationally — what's the expected cadence for a 6-week pilot? we want milestones for infra, validation, regression checks.
04:55 Sara: Typically week 1-2: staging access and smoke tests; week 3-4: load/run bench and tuning; week 5: eval on quality/regression; week 6: decision for dedicated or go-live. we'll adapt to your team's calendar.
05:18 Ravi: on billing — will the staging costs show up separately? do we need a commit for Dedicated?
05:27 Alex: hosted usage billed per-token. Dedicated is reserved capacity — we'll draft sizing & pricing recommendation. commit terms are flexible but we'll propose options.
05:40 Jordan: technical note — for the load run we'll provide a sample harness and a script that hits streaming endpoints; there may be noisy tail latencies during KV cache warm-up.
05:56 Maya: good. also, can you support function/tool calling for our ops tooling? we want the model to call internal tooling for ticket creation.
06:08 Jordan: yes, function calling supported. we'll document example payloads.
06:18 Olivia: for the VPC handoff, what connectivity artifacts do you need?
06:23 Jordan: IP ranges, CIDR for your side, any NAT/firewall rules, preferred peering window. we'll provide a template.
06:35 Ethan: and for SAML/SSO — can you integrate with Azure AD?
06:40 Sara: yes, SAML SSO with Azure AD is supported. we'll include the SSO runbook.
06:52 Maya: about data retention — some customer data must be purged after 30 days, is there a retention policy we can apply per-tenant?
07:04 Jordan: You can configure retention windows and we can set per-tenant policies in Private/Dedicated. hosted has standard retention; we'll share specifics.
07:15 Ravi: any gotchas we should be aware of during the first load run?
07:20 Jordan: watch out for bursty fan-out which can blow past KV cache effectiveness; also tokenization differences can affect per-token cost. we'll help interpret logs.
07:34 Alex: ok wrapping up — recap of next steps: i'll send security artifacts, Jordan will size pool and provide runbook, Olivia to share network details, Maya to share prompts. agree?
07:48 Maya: yes we're aligned.
07:52 Ravi: agreed. schedule the VPC deep-dive for next week.
07:57 Alex: i'll send calendar invite after this. thanks everyone.

Notes: transcription imperfect — sometimes "KV" appears as "K-V" or "key-v cache". product names occasionally shortened (Redwood Dedicated -> "Dedicated pool"). references to docs will be links in the follow-up email rather than pasted here.

End of transcript.
